skill.displayName: Pet Drying Box Heat Stress Analysis | 宠物烘干箱内热应激预警

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it claims, but it silently creates or reuses user identity state, stores tokens locally, and sends identity-linked data to remote services with limited user-facing control.

dimensions.detail: Cloud video analysis and historical report lookup fit the stated pet heat-stress analysis purpose, and the documentation discloses server-side API use and report querying.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions require automatic historical cloud queries and internal identity handling while telling the agent not to ask or show identity values, which reduces user visibility over sensitive account-scoped actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No overtly malicious install behavior was found, but the skill does not clearly declare the runtime capability surface such as network calls, local file reads, local database writes, and token persistence.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Uploading videos or URLs to the analysis API is expected, but reading workspace identity material and injecting account/platform metadata into outbound requests is broader than a narrow video-analysis task needs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The common utility creates or reuses a local default user, writes a shared SQLite database under the workspace data directory, and persists token/open-token fields without clear retention or consent controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with pet videos or video URLs being sent to lifeemergence-related APIs, historical reports being queried from the cloud, and a local workspace database storing user identifiers and service tokens. Avoid using it in shared workspaces unless you understand which identity will be reused.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr findings are generic DAO query-building risks, not actual code execution in the reviewed paths; they are not the basis for the verdict.
[LP3] unexpected: The scanner's permissions concern is supported in substance: the artifacts require network, file, environment, and local database access without a clear permissions-style disclosure.
[SDI-1] expected: The historical report list mode is documented in SKILL.md and is purpose-related, but it becomes sensitive because access is tied to silently managed identity state.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The automatic identity creation/reuse, reading data/smyx-api-key.txt, silent phoneLogin registration, and token persistence are artifact-backed and materially under-disclosed.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger language includes automatic report-query behavior; while not hidden, it could run on broad report-list requests without a fresh confirmation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The artifacts disclose remote analysis generally, but they do not adequately explain silent registration, transmitted identity fields, local token storage, or retention.
[E1] unexpected: Outbound requests to the analysis service are expected, but the separate silent registration/login POST carrying openId/mobile/source is broader than the visible pet-video workflow.
[P2] expected: The apparent hidden character occurs in an emoji sequence in SKILL.md, not as an artifact-backed hidden instruction; this was downgraded.
[YR4] expected: The metadata-poisoning signal appears tied to formatting and the emoji/description content; no concrete parser deception or malicious instruction was found.
